title: アドバンスト数理Ａ
subtitle: Advanced Mathematics A
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Engineering problems are often expressed as two-variable functions or multivariable functions. In this course, students will learn how to:
(1) derive partial derivatives.
(2) find the extreme values of two-variable functions.
(3) calculate a double integral using the iterated integral approach.
(4) calculate a double integral using the change of variables approach.
advice:
This is an advanced course following single-variable calculus and includes:

1. Multivariable functions, their limits and continuity, and partial derivatives.
2. Tangent plane and total differential for a multivariable function.
3. The chain rule in several variables.
4. Higher order partial derivatives and Taylor expansion of two-variable functions.
5. Maxima and minima of two-variable functions.
6. Iterated integration and reversing the order of integration.
7. Change of variables in a double integral.

Students are required to actively participate in class and to engage in the review and preview in every class.
Students are required to work on exercises after class and are expected to understand the contents of each class.
Students are required to explain carefully and logically the solution procedure in their homework and report.

Students should actively use the teachers' office hours and the Math. and Science Education Research Center.
books: Textbook: Advanced Mathematics A (Partial Derivative & Double Integral) [Kanazawa Institute of Technology]
requiredKnowledge: Preliminary knowledge must include an understanding of the basic mathematical concepts studied in the first year; for example, the basics of single-variable calculus and the inner and outer products of vectors learned in linear algebra.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the concepts of multivariable functions and the calculation of partial derivatives.
Be able to find partial derivatives by applying the chain rule.
Be able to find the extreme values of two-variable functions.
Be able to understand the concept of multiple integration and perform it by iterated integration.
Be able to find the value of a double integral by variable transformation, especially polar transformation.
Attend every class, make a strong effort to understand the course contents and English mathematical expressions.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1)Understand the definition of partial derivatives, and find the partial derivatives of various multivariable functions.
(2)Use the chain rule in several variables to find partial derivatives of various multivariable functions.
(3) Express the Taylor expansion of a two-variable function.
(4)Accurately evaluate the extreme values of a two-variable function.
(5)Understand the definition of multiple integrals, and accurately find multiple integrals of various functions.
(6) Use variable transformation to find multiple integrals.
